purpose: Normalize each possible lamp reading, then average the remaining book uncertainty with the probability of that reading.
meaning: Conditional entropy H(X|Y) averages the entropy of X’s conditional distribution over Y. It differs from the entropy after one selected observation. Conditioning reduces finite entropy on average, although a particular observation can increase uncertainty.

definition.setting: An assumed binary library return-tray model: X records book presence and Y records the sensor lamp.
definition.formal_latex: p_{00}=(1-q)(1-e),\quad p_{01}=(1-q)e,\quad p_{10}=qe,\quad p_{11}=q(1-e),\quad \sum_{x,y}p_{xy}=1.\quad H(X\mid Y)=\sum_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)H(X\mid Y=y),\quad H(X\mid Y=y)=-\sum_x P(X=x\mid Y=y)\log_2P(X=x\mid Y=y).

conditions: X records presence in one library return tray: 0 means empty and 1 means a book. Y records its sensor lamp: 0 means off and 1 means on. This binary presence model differs from the preceding lesson’s three possible book counts. The channel probabilities are assumed for teaching, not fitted sensor measurements.

The prior book probability q=P(X=1) and symmetric flip probability e lie in [0,1]. The same channel rule gives P(Y≠X|X=x)=e for each possible input value x; a row with zero prior mass still has a specified channel rule.
The joint masses are p₀₀=(1−q)(1−e), p₀₁=(1−q)e, p₁₀=qe and p₁₁=q(1−e). The first index belongs to X and the second to Y. All four masses are nonnegative and add to one.
Marginal distributions come from summing rows or columns. A conditional distribution given Y=y is formed only when P(Y=y)>0; then divide the selected column by its total.
The selected lamp value yₛ is a view selection. Changing it does not alter the joint distribution or any averaged entropy or mutual information.

All logarithms in these finite information quantities use base two and the unit is bits. Terms with zero joint or marginal mass are omitted from their entropy sums using the continuous zero-term convention.
H(X|Y) is the probability-weighted average of the defined slice entropies H(X|Y=y). A zero-probability column has no defined conditional distribution, and is omitted from this weighted average.
The finite entropy inequality H(X|Y)≤H(X) concerns the average over Y, not every selected value y. In this channel family H(Y|X) is the binary entropy of e.
definition.domain_notes: All displayed entropies use bits. An impossible selected observation has undefined posterior and selected entropy, while the global averaged conditional entropy remains valid.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original finite calculations; independent review pending.

grammar.expression_latex: p_{00}=(1-q)(1-e),\quad p_{01}=(1-q)e,\quad p_{10}=qe,\quad p_{11}=q(1-e),\quad \sum_{x,y}p_{xy}=1.\quad H(X\mid Y)=\sum_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)H(X\mid Y=y),\quad H(X\mid Y=y)=-\sum_x P(X=x\mid Y=y)\log_2P(X=x\mid Y=y).
grammar.formation_rule: First use q and 1−q for the book-presence probabilities. Split each row with channel probabilities 1−e and e, keeping the X index first and Y index second. Sum the joint masses across the other variable to get a marginal distribution. Divide a selected lamp column by its positive marginal total to obtain the conditional distribution. For each positive lamp marginal, compute the entropy of its normalized book distribution. Weight this slice entropy by the lamp marginal and add. A zero-probability conditioning column is omitted; its conditional distribution is not assigned a made-up value.
grammar.precedence: Multiply the prior by a channel probability to form a joint cell. Add cells to form marginals. Normalize only positive-probability conditioning columns, then apply base-two entropy formulas.

properties.claim: Average conditioning cannot increase finite entropy.
properties.conditions: Use finite random variables under one complete joint distribution.
properties.derivation: The identity H(X)−H(X|Y)=I(X;Y) and nonnegativity of mutual information give the averaged inequality. A single slice is not the average.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent mathematical review pending

properties.claim: An invertible observation leaves zero remaining uncertainty.
properties.conditions: The model makes X a deterministic function of Y on every positive-probability lamp column.
properties.derivation: Every defined conditional book distribution has a unit mass, hence entropy zero; the average is zero.
